title: Govern the Vendor Master
scenario: It is 10:00 AM. Reference data is loading. Before any payment can go out, the desk trusts one record above all others: the Vendor Master entry that says who Northwind Fasteners is and where their money goes. You do not invent this record - you govern it. Inspect V-1042 and decide what makes it trustworthy.
inputLabel: Vendor Master - V-1042 (as it stands today)
input: V-1042 | Northwind Fasteners | Remit-to: 4400 Commerce Way, Tacoma WA 98402 | Bank on file: ACH ...4021 (verified day-0) | Tax id: 91-1770045 | Status: active | Owned by: Vendor Relations Desk. This is the single record every payment to Northwind reads for the pay-to name, address, and bank account.
instructions: Treat the Vendor Master as governed reference data, not something to rewrite.
Answer the four governance questions against the record and the workflow map.
Validate to mint the vendor governance profile.

questions.prompt: Who owns and may change the Vendor Master record?

options.text: The AP Clerk, while processing each invoice
The Vendor Relations Desk, under a controlled change process
Whoever sent the most recent invoice

questions.explain: Reference data has an owner. The Vendor Relations Desk owns V-1042; the AP Clerk reads it but must never edit bank details while paying - that separation is what prevents fraud.

questions.prompt: Which field on this record most needs change control?
questions.explain: The bank account is where the money physically goes. A silent change to it is the classic payment-redirect fraud, so it carries a verified-on date and a controlled owner.

questions.prompt: Why does the payment workflow read the pay-to address from here, not from the invoice?

options.text: The invoice never lists an address
A governed master record is trusted; an invoice is an external claim that could be spoofed

questions.explain: An invoice arrives from outside and could be forged. The Vendor Master is Beacon's own verified record - reading pay-to details from it, not the document, is a control.

options.text: That this vendor may be paid without any further checks
That this vendor is approved to transact - payments to it may proceed once matched
That the vendor is new and untested

questions.explain: 'active' means the vendor is approved to transact, so a matched invoice may be paid. It does not skip matching - it just confirms the counterparty is allowed.

copilotPrompt: Explain how a vendor master record should be governed: who owns it, which fields need change control, why payments read pay-to details from it instead of the invoice, and what an active status authorizes.
successMessage: Vendor master governed. Every payment to Northwind will read this trusted record - not the invoice.

intro.heading: Before you match: trust one record

sections.title: Reference data has owners
sections.body: The Vendor Master is not yours to edit while paying. It is owned by the Vendor Relations Desk and changed only through a controlled process. You read it; you do not rewrite it.

sections.title: The bank field is the crown jewel
sections.body: Everything else on the record is descriptive. The bank account is where money lands, so it carries a verified-on date and the tightest change control on the desk.

sections.title: Why not read the invoice?
sections.body: An invoice is an external document that could be spoofed. Reading the pay-to name, address, and bank from Beacon's own governed master - never from the document - is a fraud control.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: Passing the inspection mints a vendor governance profile: proof you understand who owns the record, what needs change control, and what its status authorizes.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd match the invoice's vendor to your official vendor list and add or correct the master record if it is new or stale.

tools.powerAutomate: 'Get items' to find the vendor, then 'Update/Create item' to maintain the master
tools.zapier: 'Find or Create Record' in your vendor table
tools.python: upsert into the vendor table keyed by tax id or vendor id

takeaway.heading: Vendor master governed
points: You answered the four governance questions: owner, change-controlled field, why-not-the-invoice, and what active authorizes.
The Vendor Master is trusted reference data - the desk reads pay-to details from it, never from the incoming document.
The bank account carries the tightest change control because it is where money physically goes.
Your vendor governance profile is stored - governing reference data is a real deliverable, not overhead.
The workflow can now trust who Northwind Fasteners is and where their payments are sent.
